These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. description.narrative: (Tanzania): The objective of this project is to scale up the indoor residual spraying in Tanzania. The current geographic focus is three regions in Mainland and all 10 regions in Zanzibar. FY 2014 funds will be used to strengthen the capacity of the National and Zanzibar Malaria Control Programs to provide indoor residual spraying in the focus regions, strengthen the mobile-based reporting system for epidemic-detection and timely response in Zanzibar and establish a similar system on the Mainland; environmental compliance activities; and entomological monitoring. The expected outcomes are: interrupting malaria transmission by reducing the malaria vector population; generation of information to monitor the quality and effectiveness of spraying exercise; and protection of humans and environmental through compliance with U.S. Government regulations. This activity contributes to the President's Malaria Initiative target of reaching 85 percent of houses with indoor residual spraying and protecting 85 percent of the population.

(Tanzania): Project objectives are to improve the health status of Tanzanians by expanding the impact of targeted social marketing initiatives aligned to measurable behavioral outcomes in HIV/AIDS, family planning, reproductive health, child survival, malaria, and strengthening local capacity to sustain social marketing health activities. Activities are focused in Dar es Salaam, Dodoma, Mwanza, Arusha, Shinyanga, Mara, Manyara, and Mbeya. The project supports both the Government of Tanzania and the U.S. Government health priorities including the Global Health Initiative Strategy by increasing uptake of preventive health services and product use. Major activities include strengthening and expanding demand, access and supply of essential health commodities including oral contraceptives (OCs) to large percentages of the Tanzanian population. TSMP will strengthen research to measure willingness to pay for various commodities such as OCs and increase support to the public sector to improve condom programming. This activity has, and will continue to, result in increased access to essential health commodities for improved health outcomes

title.narrative: Southern Highlands and Ruaha-Katavi Protection Program (SHARPP)

description.narrative: (Tanzania): With the decimation of elephants in Tanzania's Selous Game Reserve, the Ruaha-Katavi landscape now harbors the largest population of elephants in eastern Africa. It is also one of the last strongholds for Africa's remaining lions. Ruaha and Katavi are two national parks separated by a large amount of healthy, but unprotected forest which is currently under threat. If this linkage between the parks is broken, the future for elephants, lions, and the livelihoods for remote rural Tanzanian communities is at risk. SHARP will use FY 2020 biodiversity funds to directly address these threats and help to protect the community lands that currently link the parks. The activity will continue working with local government authorities, community groups, and protected area managers to secure wildlife corridors on village land by providing technical assistance on sound village land-use planning sessions, and assisting local communities to form village game scout groups to patrol and prevent encroachment and poaching. It will also use FY 2020 funds to reduce human-wildlife conflict by providing training on alternative livelihoods approaches that improve economic well-being for the communities and help reduce pressure on both the ecosystem and wildlife. The activity will continue to monitor the status of key wildlife species to inform wildlife recovery and use of the secured corridors. These interventions help further Tanzania's journey to self-reliance by developing the country's own ability to monitor, preserve, and benefit from its natural resources...... .

description.narrative: Rice and maize are important staple food crops in Tanzania, produced primarily by small-scale farmers. Coordination with NAFAKA I will enable the NAFAKA II activity to scale successful innovations from NAFAKA I and intensify outreach to larger numbers of actors, primarily women and youth in the rice and maize market systems, increasing both direct and indirect beneficiaries. These market systems will lead to the successful adoption at scale of improved technologies and agricultural practices that increase overall system productivity and competitiveness, and lead to improved nutrition for these targeted smallholders. NAFAKA II activity also builds on the successful food fortification work of the USAID Tuboreshe Chakula activity, which has assisted millers to improve post-harvest handling and production and stimulate demand for fortified maize flour. Investment approaches across the activity will improve the nutritional status of Tanzanians, especially women and children; expand opportunities for benefits and participation by women, youth, and other vulnerable groups; and develop local capacity for sustaining and scaling innovation and benefits.

title.narrative: Feed the Future Enabling Growth through Investment and Enterprise (ENGINE)

description.narrative: (Tanzania): The purpose of the Enabling Growth through Investment and Enterprise activity (ENGINE) is to increase private sector investment leading to inclusive, broad-based economic growth in the Southern Agricultural Growth Corridor of Tanzania, plus Zanzibar. The development theory is that if the policy dialogue between the GOT and the private sector is strengthened to develop and implement enabling policies for investment, and the private sector has improved business skills and greater access to finance, then the binding constraints to private sector investment will be reduced, agricultural productivity and profitability will be increased and TAnzania's inclusive broad-based economic growth will be sustained. .As ENGINE enters its third year of implementation, funding will support interventions that focus at the sub-national level, using a broad-based approach and working with district councils, private sector associations, business development service providers, financial institutions, and micro, small, and medium enterprises (SMEs).
